candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care — client education, communication and discharge planning
candidate.educational_objective: Use teach-back to verify patient understanding of health instructions.

options.A: Ask, 'Do you understand?' and accept a yes response.
options.B: Provide written instructions without checking comprehension.
options.C: Ask the client to explain the key instructions in their own words using teach-back.
options.D: Assume understanding based on the client's education level.

candidate.rationale: AHRQ defines teach-back as checking understanding by asking patients to state in their own words what they need to know or do. AHRQ specifically advises against relying on yes/no questions such as 'Do you understand?' Therefore C is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Teach-back checks understanding by having the patient explain information in their own words; yes/no comprehension questions are not reliable teach-back questions.
candidate.source_document_title: Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, 3rd Edition — Use the Teach-Back Method: Tool 5
candidate.source_locator: Overview; Action — Try the teach-back method; TIP — do not ask yes/no questions
candidate.source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
candidate.stem: A nurse wants to confirm that a client understands discharge instructions. Which technique is most appropriate?
